extraction.name: MathVista
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It contains 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and three newly created datasets: IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA. It covers seven mathematical reasoning types, five primary tasks, and diverse visual contexts, with fine-grained metadata for evaluation.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.inLanguage: English, Chinese, Persian; 6.57% of questions are non-English.
extraction.citeAs: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, and Jianfeng Gao. MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. ICLR 2024. arXiv:2310.02255v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors collected 2,666 examples from nine existing math-targeted multimodal datasets. They reviewed more than 70 VQA datasets and selected 19 publicly available datasets containing math-related instances. Heuristic filtering produced 4,949 candidates, which three expert annotators assessed for mathematical reasoning; majority voting and a limit of 400 examples per source yielded 2,739 VQA examples. Three new datasets were manually curated to address additional visual reasoning scenarios: IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA. Collection guidelines emphasized task and topic diversity, varied visual contexts and mathematical skills, different difficulty levels, and deterministic evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 5,261 examples, or 85.6% of the dataset, have supplementary annotations sourced from original data providers. The limitations section explicitly identifies incomplete annotation coverage.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sources include nine existing MathQA datasets and 19 existing general VQA datasets. Collected source annotations include solutions, programs, parsing results, and grounded theorems. IQTest uses puzzle test figures from online learning platforms. FunctionQA contains questions about functional plots. PaperQA uses academic illustrations, including tables, figures, and charts from online educational resources, with 107 examples sourced from papers released in August 2023 on https://huggingface.co/papers.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each existing source dataset was limited to at most 400 examples to balance source representation. The final 6,141 examples were divided into testmini, containing 1,000 examples, and test, containing 5,141 examples. To construct testmini, questions were first randomly sampled with a threshold of four per source dataset, followed by random sampling proportional to each source's representation in the full dataset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: VQA candidates were automatically selected if they had numeric answers or questions containing quantity words from a predefined dictionary. Expert annotators then assessed mathematical reasoning relevance. Negative examples included problems involving only counting, reading or recognizing numbers, or factual recall of years and dates. Majority voting determined inclusion. Additional quality checks addressed unidentified errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three expert annotators labeled candidate VQA problems as Yes, No, or Unsure regarding mathematical reasoning, after training with detailed instructions and positive and negative examples. Annotators could flag incorrect or offensive content in comments for later removal. Questions in the three new datasets were manually annotated by STEM graduate students and independently reviewed by three reviewers; answer disagreements were resolved through team discussion. Dataset metadata includes question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, visual context, and mathematical reasoning types. Metadata and coarse reasoning labels were obtained from source dataset details, and expert annotators manually checked reasoning labels for 1,000 examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom GUI annotation tools were developed for identifying mathematical problems, annotating the three new datasets, and labeling mathematical reasoning skills. Amazon Mechanical Turk was used separately for the human performance baseline and assessment of Bard predictions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Majority voting combined the three expert judgments for VQA candidate inclusion. Inter-annotator agreement for identifying mathematical reasoning had a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775. Review of the 736 newly collected questions yielded 99.2% answer consistency, with six disagreements resolved through discussion to consensus. Automatic reasoning-category annotations matched human annotations exactly at the example level for 94.1% of 1,000 checked examples, and 98.79% of individual labels were identical. The testmini distribution had KL divergence of 0.008 and total variation distance of 0.035 from the full dataset.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three expert judgments per VQA candidate for mathematical-reasoning inclusion; three independent reviewers for the new datasets. Separately, each testmini question was assigned to five annotators for the human performance baseline.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Questions in the new datasets were annotated by graduate students in STEM fields. Human-performance annotators were required to have a high school diploma or higher, more than 5,000 completed HIT tasks, an acceptance score above 0.99, and successful completion of qualification questions.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automatic metadata and coarse mathematical-reasoning labeling based on source dataset details; no named annotation software or model is specified for these labels.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Answer labels for the test subset will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination, and the authors will maintain an online evaluation platform. They commit to maintaining the datasets, refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard as new models emerge. Future iterations are intended to broaden problem and visual-context coverage and provide unified, comprehensive annotations. No update schedule, versioning policy, or deprecation policy is specified.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Dataset examples include identifiable public figures, named entities, biographical ages or birth dates, and age-gap questions. Example statistical figures contain gender, educational-attainment, and political-affiliation categories. Separately, human-performance annotators were asked to report their highest educational attainment.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to support development of general-purpose AI assistants capable of mathematical reasoning in visually intensive real-world scenarios. The paper discusses potential applications in education, analysis of statistical data, theorem proving, and scientific discovery. Grade-level categorization is intended to help assess models' practical utility and educational relevance.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Coverage may omit some mathematical problem types and visual contexts. Collection of high-quality visual mathematical reasoning data is labor-intensive, raising concerns about scalability and generalizability to other domains. Only 85.6% of examples have supplementary annotations, and heterogeneous source annotations lack a unified format and structure. The paper also presents low-resolution figures, ambiguous visual contexts, and an example described as incomplete or requiring implicit measuring ability.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and benchmarking mathematical reasoning of LLMs and LMMs in visual contexts, including fine-grained analysis across tasks, mathematical reasoning types, visual contexts, and grade levels. The 1,000-example testmini subset is intended for model-development validation and evaluation with limited computing resources; the 5,141-example test subset is intended for standard evaluation. Collected source annotations can provide demonstration examples for LLMs. The benchmark also supports research on zero-shot and few-shot prompting, tool augmentation, self-verification, self-consistency, and multi-turn human-AI interaction.
